review_output.summary: [High] convertfourslash and updatefailing crash with ENOENT: manualTests.txt is never created, and *.txt is gitignored
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: the change doesn't add manualTests.txt, and getManualTests() reads it with readFileSync and no existence check. By the time that read throws, main() has already deleted tests/gen, so `npm run convertfourslash` leaves the generated tests wiped. `npm run updatefailing` has also already emptied failingTests.txt (updateFailing.mts:10) before it crashes the same way. On top of that, .gitignore:176 ignores `*.txt` and only failingTests.txt is excepted (.gitignore:200), so a manualTests.txt that makemanual writes is silently left untracked. Remedy: commit an empty manualTests.txt, add `!internal/fourslash/_scripts/manualTests.txt` to .gitignore, and have getManualTests return an empty set when the file is missing, as makeManual.mts already does.

review_output.summary: [High] makeManual writes a different name to manualTests.txt than convertFourslash looks up, so manual tests are never skipped
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: makeManual uses args[0] directly as the file name in tests/gen, with no suffix added. So only the full file name (e.g. `fooBar_test.go`) passes its existence check, and that exact string is what gets written to manualTests.txt. convertFourslash.mts:70-72 compares against the capitalized name with no suffix (`FooBar`). Passing `FooBar` makes makeManual fail with "Test file not found". Either way the skip never fires, and the next convertfourslash run regenerates the test in tests/gen next to the manual copy. The entry format also doesn't match failingTests.txt, which uses `TestXxx`. Remedy: pick one key format (e.g. `TestXxx`), have makeManual derive the gen file name from it, and compare using the same derivation in convertFourslash, reusing generateGoTest's name logic.

review_output.summary: [High] Tests moved to tests/manual/ have no util_test.go helpers, so the manual package does not compile
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: generateHelperFile() copies util_test.go (ptrTo, defaultCommitCharacters, completionGlobals, ...) only into tests/gen. About 610 generated tests use these helpers. When makeManual moves one into tests/manual, that directory is its own Go package with no helper definitions, so `go test ./internal/fourslash/tests/manual` (and `./...`) fails with undefined identifiers. Remedy: also copy util_test.go into tests/manual in generateHelperFile() or makeManual, or move the helpers into a shared package both directories can import.

review_output.summary: [Medium] A test skipped as failing keeps its t.Skip() after it moves to manual, and updatefailing never checks it again
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: makeManual moves the generated file unchanged, including any `t.Skip()` added for tests in failingTests.txt (convertFourslash.mts:968). updatefailing only runs `go test ./internal/fourslash/tests/gen` (updateFailing.mts:15), so nothing ever un-skips the manual test. It silently runs nothing while looking like coverage. Remedy: strip the generated t.Skip() when moving the file (or warn/refuse), or extend updateFailing to run tests/manual too.

review_output.summary: [Medium] List-file parsing now exists three times, and the copies disagree on whether a missing file is allowed
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: the readFileSync/split/trim/filter pipeline is hand-written at convertFourslash.mts:22, convertFourslash.mts:27 and makeManual.mts:36, and the copies have already drifted: makeManual tolerates a missing file, getManualTests does not. makeManual.mts also re-declares the manualTests path and the gen/manual directory constants that convertFourslash.mts owns. Any change to the list format has to be made in three places. Remedy: export one `readTestList(path, transform?)` helper from convertFourslash.mts that returns an empty set for a missing file, build getFailingTests and getManualTests on it, and import it plus the path constants in makeManual.mts, the same way updateFailing.mts already imports from convertFourslash.mts.

review_output.summary: [Low] Test-name capitalization is copied from generateGoTest
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: the key used to skip manual tests (line 70) and the one generateGoTest uses for the Test name and failing-test lookup (line 946) are computed separately. If one changes, manual skipping silently stops lining up with the generated names. Remedy: compute testName once (a getTestName/capitalize helper, or a field on GoTest) and pass it to generateGoTest.

review_output.summary: [Low] Dead `if (testContent)` check on a function that always returns a non-empty string
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: generateGoTest (line 945) is typed to return string and always returns a non-empty template, so the new guard can never be false. It suggests a "no output" path that doesn't exist. Remedy: remove the `if (testContent)` wrapper and write the file unconditionally, as before.

review_output.summary: [Low] convertfourslash creates tests/manual on every run although it never writes there
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: manualOutputDir is only ever passed to mkdirSync. convertFourslash neither writes to it nor formats it (gofumpt runs only on tests/gen), and makeManual already creates the directory itself, so two scripts now manage the same directory. Remedy: remove manualOutputDir and its mkdirSync from convertFourslash.mts, unless it's repurposed to copy util_test.go there (see the tests/manual helpers finding).

review_output.summary: [Low] makemanual with no argument exits 1 with no usage message
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: `npm run makemanual` with no argument fails with only npm's generic error and no hint about what to pass. Given the confusion over the name format, users are likely to guess wrong. Remedy: print a usage line, e.g. `console.error("Usage: npm run makemanual -- <testName>")`, before process.exit(1).

review_output.summary: [Nitpick] Redundant alias, no-op template literal and redundant existsSync in makeManual
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: `testFileName` just copies `testName`, `${testFileName}` is the same string, and `mkdirSync(..., { recursive: true })` already does nothing when the directory exists, so the existsSync check adds noise. Remedy: use testName directly, drop the template literal, and call mkdirSync without the existsSync guard.

## Verdict: BLOCK (code)

Spec: skipped, no spec found.

Coverage (self-reported): 3 of 3 changed files examined by at least one reviewer.

Verification: 5 checked (4 stand, 1 partly refuted, 0 refuted), 0 not checked. Spec findings are not verified.

### High
- **[High] `internal/fourslash/_scripts/convertFourslash.mts:27`: `convertfourslash` and `updatefailing` crash because `manualTests.txt` doesn't exist, and `*.txt` files are gitignored**
  - **Impact:** The change doesn't add `manualTests.txt`, and `getManualTests()` reads it with `readFileSync` without checking that it exists.
    - Before that read throws, `main()` has already deleted `tests/gen`. So `npm run convertfourslash` leaves the generated tests wiped.
    - `npm run updatefailing` has also already emptied `failingTests.txt` (`updateFailing.mts:10`) by the time it crashes.
    - `.gitignore:176` ignores `*.txt`, and only `failingTests.txt` is re-included (`.gitignore:200`). So a `manualTests.txt` that `makemanual` creates is silently left out of git.
  - **Remedy:** Commit an empty `manualTests.txt` and add `!internal/fourslash/_scripts/manualTests.txt` to `.gitignore`. Also make `getManualTests` return an empty set when the file is missing, as `makeManual.mts` already does.
  - flagged by: correctness, ai-antipatterns
  - verification: verified

- **[High] `internal/fourslash/_scripts/makeManual.mts:16`: `makeManual` writes a different name to `manualTests.txt` than `convertFourslash` looks up, so manual tests are never skipped**
  - **Impact:** The two scripts use different names for the same test.
    - `makeManual` uses the argument as-is as a file name in `tests/gen`. Only the full file name (`fooBar_test.go`) passes its existence check, and that exact string goes into the list.
    - `convertFourslash.mts:70` looks up the capitalized name with no suffix (`FooBar`). Passing `FooBar` to `makeManual` fails with "Test file not found".
    - Either way the skip never happens. The next `convertfourslash` run regenerates the test in `tests/gen` next to the manual copy.
    - The entry format also doesn't match `failingTests.txt`, which uses `TestXxx`.
  - **Remedy:** Pick one name format for entries. Have `makeManual` work out the file name from it, and have `convertFourslash` compare using the same rule.
  - flagged by: correctness, ai-antipatterns, craft, dry, tests
  - verification: verified

- **[High] `internal/fourslash/_scripts/makeManual.mts:30`: tests moved to `tests/manual/` lose the `util_test.go` helpers, so that package won't compile**
  - **Impact:** `generateHelperFile()` copies `util_test.go` only into `tests/gen`.
    - About 610 generated tests use its helpers (`ptrTo`, `completionGlobals`, `defaultCommitCharacters`).
    - In Go, each directory is its own package. A moved test that uses these helpers breaks `go test ./internal/fourslash/tests/manual` and `./...`.
  - **Remedy:** Also copy `util_test.go` into `tests/manual`, or move the helpers into a shared package both directories can import.
  - flagged by: tests, correctness
  - verification: verified. The verifier didn't run `go build`, so the compile failure itself is unchecked; it follows from Go's one-package-per-directory rule.

### Medium
- **[Medium] `internal/fourslash/_scripts/makeManual.mts:31`: a test skipped as failing keeps its `t.Skip()` after moving to manual, and `updatefailing` never checks it again**
  - **Impact:** The file is moved unchanged, including any generated `t.Skip()`. `updatefailing` only runs `tests/gen`, so the manual test stays skipped and silently runs nothing.
  - **Remedy:** Strip the generated `t.Skip()` when moving the file (or warn), or have `updateFailing` also run `tests/manual`.
  - verification: partly refuted. The claim that the test's entry stays in `failingTests.txt` is false: `updateFailing.mts:10` clears the file and line 28 rebuilds it from `tests/gen` only. The core defect stands.

- **[Medium] `internal/fourslash/_scripts/convertFourslash.mts:26`: the code that reads a list file now exists three times, and the copies disagree on whether a missing file is allowed**
  - **Impact:** The copies are at `convertFourslash.mts:22` and `:27`, and `makeManual.mts:36`. `makeManual.mts` also redefines path constants that `convertFourslash.mts` already has, and the copies have already drifted apart.
  - **Remedy:** Export one `readTestList(path, transform?)` helper that returns an empty set for a missing file, and import it in `makeManual.mts`. `updateFailing.mts` already imports from `convertFourslash.mts`, so this follows an existing pattern.
  - flagged by: craft, dry, ai-antipatterns
  - verification: verified

### Low
- **[Low] `convertFourslash.mts:70`: the test-name capitalization is copied from `generateGoTest` (line 946).** Remedy: compute the name once and pass it in. (craft, dry)
- **[Low] `convertFourslash.mts:76`: the `if (testContent)` check can never be false**, because `generateGoTest` always returns a non-empty string. Remedy: remove the guard. (ai-antipatterns, craft)
- **[Low] `convertFourslash.mts:44`: every run creates `tests/manual`, but `convertFourslash` never writes there.** Remedy: remove the `mkdirSync`, or use that directory to hold the helper copy. (ai-antipatterns, craft)
- **[Low] `makeManual.mts:12`: running with no argument exits with code 1 and no message.** Remedy: print a usage line first. (correctness)

### Nitpick
- **[Nitpick] `makeManual.mts:17`: unnecessary code.** The `testFileName` alias just copies `testName`, the template literal changes nothing, and the `existsSync` check is unnecessary before `mkdirSync({recursive:true})`. (ai-antipatterns)

### Refuted in verification
None.
